overview.description: Plasmids are like plugins for a cell - files you attach to change its function. But as the saying goes, synbio is 'like writing code inside a burrito': thousands of intersecting messages mean a change can cascade unpredictably, even killing the cell while it makes your protein.
objectives: describe plasmid elements (ORI, resistance, MCS, promoter)

steps.intro: Plasmids are like plugins for a cell - files you attach to change its function. But as the saying goes, synbio is 'like writing code inside a burrito': thousands of intersecting messages mean a change can cascade unpredictably, even killing the cell while it makes your protein.

instructions.title: Learn the parts
instructions.description: Study the ORI, antibiotic-resistance gene, multiple cloning site and promoter, and what each does.

instructions.title: Understand copy number
instructions.description: High-copy plasmids give more yield but more burden; pick based on your goal.

instructions.title: Beware catastrophic success
instructions.description: Recognise that over-expression can kill cells. Inducible systems mitigate this.

submission.description: Summarise the function of each major plasmid element in your own words and identify them on a real plasmid map.

kits.name: Plasmid map viewer (free)
kits.note: Design and annotate plasmids in the browser - identify ori, marker, MCS.

kits.name: Plasmids from the repository
kits.note: Real, sequence-verified plasmids for registered labs/community spaces.
